Type 1 is a general category so different "Type 1" paitents can have very different rootcauses for the condition even if the net symptom is ultimatly the same. Sometimes it's simply not enough insulin produced, sometimes it's a genetic abnormality that causes errors in their insulin produced so it comes out non-functional.

Type 2 is as you said is insulin resistance, genetic factors do predispose certain people twoards it, but it's still a 100% caused by excess bodyfat and poor diet, hence why it's unheard of in skinny/fit people and even "normal" people with moderate bodyfat only make up 15% of Type 2 paitents.

Thankfully though, treating Type 1 diabetes is usually as simple as replacing the missing insulin, the hard part though is that it's reliant on the individual/family to constantly monitor and manage the blood sugar. Compared to a generation ago the prognosis for a kid with Type 1 is way better because modern digital equipment has made managing diabetes much easier/quicker/painless/precise than drawing blood with a needle, dipping a test strip, deciding which color the strip matches up with, and doing the math for a dosage.
